BiblicalUsage: Saraph is burning, and it burns what must be destroyed. David burned the gods the Philistines left behind at Baal-perazim; Pharaoh took Gezer and burnt it with fire; the Amalekites burned Ziklag, and David came back to find the city burned with fire and the wives and children taken captive.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fire in Scripture is never neutral: it destroys what is false, and it tests what remains. The burning of idols and the burning of cities both say the same thing — what stands against God does not last. And I hold that the God who burns away the false is the same God who spares His people through the fire.
